sanskrit: na mām arhasi gāndhāri doṣeṇa pariśaṅkitum anigṛhya purā putrān asmāsv anapakāriṣu
english: You ought not, Gāndhārī, to suspect me of wrongdoing, for in the past you did not restrain your sons when they offended against us who had done them no harm.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca vṛddhasyāsya śataṃ putrān nighnaṃs tvam aparājitaḥ kasmān na śeṣayaḥ kaṃ cid yenālpam aparādhitam
english: Gāndhārī said: Slaying the hundred sons of this aged man, you who were never vanquished—why did you not spare even one, even him whose offense was slight?

sanskrit: saṃtānam āvayos tāta vṛddhayor hṛtarājyayoḥ katham andhadvayasyāsya yaṣṭir ekā na varjitā
english: Why, child, was not a single staff left for us two—aged, robbed of our kingdom—the one prop of this blind pair, to continue our line?

sanskrit: śeṣe hy avasthite tāta putrāṇām antake tvayi na me duḥkhaṃ bhaved etad yadi tvaṃ dharmam ācaraḥ
english: Had but one remained, child, even with you the destroyer of my sons still standing, this grief would not be mine—if only you had acted according to dharma.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu gāndhārī yudhiṣṭhiram apṛcchata kva sa rājeti sakrodhā putrapautravadhārditā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Gāndhārī, in her wrath, tormented by the slaughter of her sons and grandsons, asked Yudhiṣṭhira: "Where is the king?"

sanskrit: tām abhyagacchad rājendro vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ yudhiṣṭhira idaṃ caināṃ madhuraṃ vākyam abravīt
english: The lord of kings, Yudhiṣṭhira, came toward her trembling, his palms joined in reverence, and spoke to her these gentle words:

sanskrit: putrahantā nṛśaṃso 'haṃ tava devi yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śāpārhaḥ pṛthivīnāśe hetubhūtaḥ śapasva mām
english: "I am Yudhiṣṭhira, O queen, the cruel slayer of your sons, deserving of your curse, the cause of the earth's destruction. Curse me."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitenārtho na rājyena dhanena vā tādṛśān suhṛdo hatvā mūḍhasyāsya suhṛddruhaḥ
english: "I, a fool and a betrayer of friends, who have slain such kinsmen as these—I have no use for life, nor for kingdom, nor for wealth."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ bhītaṃ saṃnikarṣagataṃ tadā novāca kiṃ cid gāndhārī niḥśvāsaparamā bhṛśam
english: To him who spoke thus, frightened and come close before her, Gāndhārī said nothing at all, only drawing the deepest and most labored of sighs.

sanskrit: tasyāvanatadehasya pādayor nipatiṣyataḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya nṛpater dharmajñā dharmadarśinī aṅgulyagrāṇi dadṛśe devī paṭṭāntareṇa sā
english: As King Yudhiṣṭhira, his body bowed low, was about to fall at her feet, the queen—knower of dharma, beholder of dharma—glimpsed the tips of his toes through the edge of her blindfold.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kunakībhūto darśanīyanakho nṛpaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā cārjuno 'gacchad vāsudevasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: At that the king, whose nails had been comely, became deformed of nail; and Arjuna, seeing it, withdrew to take cover behind Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃceṣṭamānāṃs tān itaś cetaś ca bhārata gāndhārī vigatakrodhā sāntvayām āsa mātṛvat
english: As they shifted about thus, this way and that, O Bhārata, Gāndhārī, her anger now departed, consoled them like a mother.

sanskrit: tayā te samanujñātā mātaraṃ vīramātaram abhyagacchanta sahitāḥ pṛthāṃ pṛthulavakṣasaḥ
english: Dismissed by her with her leave, those broad-chested heroes went together to their mother Pṛthā, the mother of heroes.

sanskrit: cirasya dṛṣṭvā putrān sā putrādhibhir abhiplutā bāṣpam āhārayad devī vastreṇāvṛtya vai mukham
english: Beholding her sons after so long a time, overwhelmed by anguish for her sons, the lady let her tears flow, veiling her face with her garment.

sanskrit: tato bāṣpaṃ samutsṛjya saha putrais tathā pṛthā apaśyad etāñ śastraughair bahudhā parivikṣatān
english: Then, having wept her tears with her sons, Pṛthā saw them mangled in many places by the floods of weapons.

sanskrit: sā tān ekaikaśaḥ putrān saṃspṛśantī punaḥ punaḥ anvaśocanta duḥkhārtā draupadīṃ ca hatātmajām rudatīm atha pāñcālīṃ dadarśa patitāṃ bhuvi
english: Touching her sons one by one again and again, stricken with grief she lamented; and then she saw Draupadī, the Pāñcāla princess bereft of her sons, weeping, fallen upon the ground.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca ārye pautrāḥ kva te sarve saubhadrasahitā gatāḥ na tvāṃ te 'dyābhigacchanti ciradṛṣṭāṃ tapasvinīm kiṃ nu rājyena vai kāryaṃ vihīnāyāḥ sutair mama
english: Draupadī said: "Noble lady, where have all your grandsons gone, together with the son of Subhadrā? They do not come to you today, you whom they had not seen so long, you the patient sufferer. What use, then, is a kingdom to me, who am bereft of my sons?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tāṃ samāśvāsayām āsa pṛthā pṛthulalocanā utthāpya yājñasenīṃ tu rudatīṃ śokakarśitām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The large-eyed Pṛthā comforted her, raising up the daughter of Yajñasena as she wept, wasted with sorrow.

sanskrit: tayaiva sahitā cāpi putrair anugatā pṛthā abhyagacchata gāndhārīm ārtām ārtatarā svayam
english: Then, together with her and followed by her sons, Pṛthā—herself more anguished still—came to the grieving Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tām uvācātha gāndhārī saha vadhvā yaśasvinīm maivaṃ putrīti śokārtā paśya mām api duḥkhitām
english: Then Gāndhārī, stricken with sorrow, said to that illustrious lady who had come with her daughter-in-law: "Do not grieve so, my daughter; look upon me too, who am sorrowing."

sanskrit: manye lokavināśo 'yaṃ kālaparyāyacoditaḥ avaśyabhāvī saṃprāptaḥ svabhāvāl lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: "I deem this destruction of the world, impelled by the turning of time, was bound to come; it has arrived of its own nature, making the hair stand on end."

sanskrit: idaṃ tat samanuprāptaṃ vidurasya vaco mahat asiddhānunaye kṛṣṇe yad uvāca mahāmatiḥ
english: "This has now come to pass—that great word of Vidura which the wise one spoke when Kṛṣṇa's mission of conciliation had failed."

sanskrit: tasminn aparihārye 'rthe vyatīte ca viśeṣataḥ mā śuco na hi śocyās te saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: "In a matter that could not be averted, and that especially is now past, do not grieve; for those who have met their death in battle are not to be mourned."

sanskrit: yathaiva tvaṃ tathaivāhaṃ ko vā māśvāsayiṣyati mamaiva hy aparādhena kulam agryaṃ vināśitam
english: "As you are, so am I; and who is there to console me? For it is through my own fault that this foremost lineage has been destroyed."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu gāndhārī kurūṇām āvikartanam apaśyat tatra tiṣṭhantī sarvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Gāndhārī, standing there, beheld the whole slaughter of the Kurus with her divine eye.

sanskrit: pativratā mahābhāgā samānavratacāriṇī ugreṇa tapasā yuktā satataṃ satyavādinī
english: Devoted to her husband, greatly blessed, sharing in his vows, endowed with fierce austerity, ever truthful of speech—

sanskrit: varadānena kṛṣṇasya maharṣeḥ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ divyajñānabalopetā vividhaṃ paryadevayat
english: by the boon of the great sage Kṛṣṇa of holy deeds, gifted with the power of divine sight, she lamented in many ways.

sanskrit: dadarśa sā buddhimatī dūrād api yathāntike raṇājiraṃ nṛvīrāṇām adbhutaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: That wise lady beheld, even from afar as if it were close at hand, the battlefield of the heroes of men, wondrous and hair-raising.

sanskrit: asthikeśaparistīrṇaṃ śoṇitaughapariplutam śarīrair bahusāhasrair vinikīrṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: strewn over with bones and hair, flooded with torrents of blood, scattered on every side with bodies in their many thousands;

sanskrit: gajāśvarathayodhānām āvṛtaṃ rudhirāvilaiḥ śarīrair aśiraskaiś ca videhaiś ca śirogaṇaiḥ
english: covered with the blood-soaked bodies of elephants, horses, chariots, and warriors, with headless trunks and with masses of heads severed from their bodies;

sanskrit: gajāśvanaravīrāṇāṃ niḥsattvair abhisaṃvṛtam sṛgālabaḍakākolakaṅkakākaniṣevitam
english: thick with the lifeless forms of heroes among elephants, horses, and men, frequented by jackals, crows, ravens, herons, and carrion-birds;

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ puruṣādānāṃ modanaṃ kurarākulam aśivābhiḥ śivābhiś ca nāditaṃ gṛdhrasevitam
english: a place of delight for the man-eating rākṣasas, swarming with ospreys, made to resound by ill-omened she-jackals, and haunted by vultures.

sanskrit: tato vyāsābhyanujñāto dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ pāṇḍuputrāś ca te sarve yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ
english: Then King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with Vyāsa's leave, and all the sons of Pāṇḍu with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head,

sanskrit: vāsudevaṃ puraskṛtya hatabandhuṃ ca pārthivam kurustriyaḥ samāsādya jagmur āyodhanaṃ prati
english: placing Vāsudeva before them, together with the king whose kinsmen had been slain, joined by the women of the Kurus, set out toward the field of battle.

sanskrit: samāsādya kurukṣetraṃ tāḥ striyo nihateśvarāḥ apaśyanta hatāṃs tatra putrān bhrātṝn pitṝn patīn
english: Reaching Kurukṣetra, those women whose lords had been slain saw lying there their sons, their brothers, their fathers, and their husbands, all slaughtered—

sanskrit: kravyādair bhakṣyamāṇān vai gomāyubaḍavāyasaiḥ bhūtaiḥ piśācai rakṣobhir vividhaiś ca niśācaraiḥ
english: being devoured by beasts of prey, by jackals, ravens, and crows, by goblins, piśācas, rākṣasas, and the many kinds of night-roaming creatures.

sanskrit: rudrākrīḍanibhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā viśasanaṃ striyaḥ mahārhebhyo 'tha yānebhyo vikrośantyo nipetire
english: Beholding then that carnage, like the playground of Rudra, the women, crying aloud, threw themselves down from their costly chariots.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ paśyantyo duḥkhārtā bharatastriyaḥ śarīreṣv askhalann anyā nyapataṃś cāparā bhuvi
english: Seeing what they had never seen before, the women of the Bharatas, stricken with grief, stumbled upon the bodies—some of them—while others fell to the ground.

sanskrit: śrāntānāṃ cāpy anāthānāṃ nāsīt kā cana cetanā pāñcālakuruyoṣāṇāṃ kṛpaṇaṃ tad abhūn mahat
english: In the women of the Pāñcālas and Kurus, exhausted and now without protectors, there remained no consciousness at all; great and pitiable was that scene.

sanskrit: duḥkhopahatacittābhiḥ samantād anunāditam dṛṣṭvāyodhanam atyugraṃ dharmajñā subalātmajā
english: As the place rang out on every side with the cries of women whose minds were shattered by grief, the knower of dharma, the daughter of Subala, gazed upon that fearful battlefield.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā puṇḍarīkākṣam āmantrya puruṣottamam kurūṇāṃ vaiśasaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhād vacanam abravīt
english: Then, addressing the lotus-eyed one, the supreme among men, and beholding the slaughter of the Kurus, she spoke out of her grief these words:

sanskrit: paśyaitāḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa snuṣā me nihateśvarāḥ prakīrṇakeśāḥ krośantīḥ kurarīr iva mādhava
english: "Behold, lotus-eyed one, these daughters-in-law of mine, their lords slain, their hair dishevelled, shrieking like ospreys, O Mādhava!"

sanskrit: amūs tv abhisamāgamya smarantyo bharatarṣabhān pṛthag evābhyadhāvanta putrān bhrātṝn pitṝn patīn
english: "These women, having come together and remembering the bulls of the Bharatas, run, each apart, toward their sons, their brothers, their fathers, their husbands."

sanskrit: vīrasūbhir mahābāho hataputrābhir āvṛtam kva cic ca vīrapatnībhir hatavīrābhir ākulam
english: "The field, O mighty-armed one, is covered with mothers of heroes whose sons are slain, and here and there crowded with wives of heroes whose heroes are slain."

sanskrit: śobhitaṃ puruṣavyāghrair bhīṣmakarṇābhimanyubhiḥ droṇadrupadaśalyaiś ca jvaladbhir iva pāvakaiḥ
english: "It is adorned with those tigers among men—Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Abhimanyu, and Droṇa, Drupada, and Śalya—who are like blazing fires."

sanskrit: kāñcanaiḥ kavacair niṣkair maṇibhiś ca mahātmanām aṅgadair hastakeyūraiḥ sragbhiś ca samalaṃkṛtam
english: "It is bedecked with the golden armor, the necklaces, the gems, the armlets, the bracelets, and the garlands of those great souls."

sanskrit: vīrabāhuvisṛṣṭābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ parighair api khaḍgaiś ca vimalais tīkṣṇaiḥ saśaraiś ca śarāsanaiḥ
english: "with the spears hurled from heroes' arms, with iron clubs, with swords bright and keen, and with bows still strung with arrows;"

sanskrit: kravyādasaṃghair muditais tiṣṭhadbhiḥ sahitaiḥ kva cit kva cid ākrīḍamānaiś ca śayānair aparaiḥ kva cit
english: "with throngs of carrion-beasts, joyful, standing together here, sporting there, and elsewhere lying at rest."

sanskrit: etad evaṃvidhaṃ vīra saṃpaśyāyodhanaṃ vibho paśyamānā ca dahyāmi śokenāhaṃ janārdana
english: "Look, O hero, O lord, upon this battlefield of such a kind; and as I look, I am consumed with grief, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca vināśaṃ madhusūdana pañcānām iva bhūtānāṃ nāhaṃ vadham acintayam
english: "The destruction of the Pāñcālas and the Kurus, O slayer of Madhu—like that of the five elements themselves—I had never imagined."

sanskrit: tān suparṇāś ca gṛdhrāś ca niṣkarṣanty asṛgukṣitān nigṛhya kavaceṣūgrā bhakṣayanti sahasraśaḥ
english: "Eagles and vultures drag those blood-drenched bodies, and seizing them fiercely by their armor, devour them in their thousands."

sanskrit: jayadrathasya karṇasya tathaiva droṇabhīṣmayoḥ abhimanyor vināśaṃ ca kaś cintayitum arhati
english: "Who could have imagined the destruction of Jayadratha, of Karṇa, and likewise of Droṇa and Bhīṣma, and of Abhimanyu?"

sanskrit: avadhyakalpān nihatān dṛṣṭvāhaṃ madhusūdana gṛdhrakaṅkabaḍaśyenaśvasṛgālādanīkṛtān
english: "Beholding them slain, O slayer of Madhu—they who seemed as if unslayable—made the food of vultures, herons, crows, hawks, dogs, and jackals,"

sanskrit: amarṣavaśam āpannān duryodhanavaśe sthitān paśyemān puruṣavyāghrān saṃśāntān pāvakān iva
english: "behold these tigers among men, who had fallen under the sway of wrath and stood under Duryodhana's command, now stilled like extinguished fires."

sanskrit: śayanāny ucitāḥ sarve mṛdūni vimalāni ca vipannās te 'dya vasudhāṃ vivṛtām adhiśerate
english: "All accustomed to beds soft and spotless, fallen now, today they lie upon the bare earth."

sanskrit: bandibhiḥ satataṃ kāle stuvadbhir abhinanditāḥ śivānām aśivā ghorāḥ śṛṇvanti vividhā giraḥ
english: "Forever gladdened in due season by bards who sang their praises, they now hear the inauspicious, dreadful cries of the she-jackals in their many tones."

sanskrit: ye purā śerate vīrāḥ śayaneṣu yaśasvinaḥ candanāgurudigdhāṅgās te 'dya pāṃsuṣu śerate
english: "Those glorious heroes who once lay upon couches, their limbs anointed with sandal and aloe, today lie in the dust."

sanskrit: teṣām ābharaṇāny ete gṛdhragomāyuvāyasāḥ ākṣipanty aśivā ghorā vinadantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "These vultures, jackals, and crows, ill-omened and dreadful, screaming again and again, tear away their ornaments."

sanskrit: cāpāni viśikhān pītān nistriṃśān vimalā gadāḥ yuddhābhimāninaḥ prītā jīvanta iva bibhrati
english: "Proud in battle, they bear still, as if alive and glad, their bows, their burnished arrows, their swords, and their gleaming maces."

sanskrit: surūpavarṇā bahavaḥ kravyādair avaghaṭṭitāḥ ṛṣabhapratirūpākṣāḥ śerate haritasrajaḥ
english: "Many of fair form and hue, mauled by the carrion-beasts, with eyes like a bull's, lie there wearing their fresh garlands."

sanskrit: apare punar āliṅgya gadāḥ parighabāhavaḥ śerate 'bhimukhāḥ śūrā dayitā iva yoṣitaḥ
english: "Others again, brave men whose arms were like iron bars, lie embracing their maces, turned toward them as toward beloved women."

sanskrit: bibhrataḥ kavacāny anye vimalāny āyudhāni ca na dharṣayanti kravyādā jīvantīti janārdana
english: "Still others bear their bright armor and their weapons, and the carrion-beasts do not assail them, thinking them alive, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: kravyādaiḥ kṛṣyamāṇānām apareṣāṃ mahātmanām śātakaumbhyaḥ srajaś citrā viprakīrṇāḥ samantataḥ
english: "Of other great-souled warriors, dragged about by the carrion-beasts, the bright garlands of pure gold lie scattered on every side."

sanskrit: ete gomāyavo bhīmā nihatānāṃ yaśasvinām kaṇṭhāntaragatān hārān ākṣipanti sahasraśaḥ
english: "These dreadful jackals tear away by the thousand the necklaces that lay upon the throats of the glorious slain."

sanskrit: sarveṣv apararātreṣu yān anandanta bandinaḥ stutibhiś ca parārdhyābhir upacāraiś ca śikṣitāḥ
english: "Those whom the bards in every last watch of night used to gladden with their praises and with their trained and choicest attendance—"

sanskrit: tān imāḥ paridevanti duḥkhārtāḥ paramāṅganāḥ kṛpaṇaṃ vṛṣṇiśārdūla duḥkhaśokārditā bhṛśam
english: "these noble women, stricken with grief, lament them piteously, O tiger of the Vṛṣṇis, sorely tormented by pain and sorrow."

sanskrit: raktotpalavanānīva vibhānti rucirāṇi vai mukhāni paramastrīṇāṃ pariśuṣkāṇi keśava
english: "Like beds of red lotuses the lovely faces of those noble women shine forth, parched and withered now, O Keśava."

sanskrit: ruditoparatā hy etā dhyāyantyaḥ saṃpariplutāḥ kurustriyo 'bhigacchanti tena tenaiva duḥkhitāḥ
english: "Their weeping spent, brooding and wholly overwhelmed, these women of the Kurus, sorrowing, go now this way, now that."

sanskrit: etāny ādityavarṇāni tapanīyanibhāni ca roṣarodanatāmrāṇi vaktrāṇi kuruyoṣitām
english: "These faces of the women of the Kurus, of the hue of the sun and like refined gold, are flushed coppery red with anger and with weeping."

sanskrit: āsām aparipūrṇārthaṃ niśamya paridevitam itaretarasaṃkrandān na vijānanti yoṣitaḥ
english: "Hearing one another's broken, unfinished laments and their mingled wailing, the women cannot make out the meaning of it."

sanskrit: etā dīrgham ivocchvasya vikruśya ca vilapya ca vispandamānā duḥkhena vīrā jahati jīvitam
english: "These women, after sighing long, after crying out and lamenting, writhing in their grief, the brave ones give up their very lives."

sanskrit: bahvyo dṛṣṭvā śarīrāṇi krośanti vilapanti ca pāṇibhiś cāparā ghnanti śirāṃsi mṛdupāṇayaḥ
english: "Many, seeing the bodies, shriek and lament; and others, soft of hand, beat their heads with their hands."

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ patitair hastaiḥ sarvāṅgair yūthaśaḥ kṛtaiḥ itaretarasaṃpṛktair ākīrṇā bhāti medinī
english: "With fallen heads, with hands, with limbs of every kind heaped together in masses and tangled one with another, the earth lies strewn and gleaming."

sanskrit: viśiraskān atho kāyān dṛṣṭvā ghorābhinandinaḥ muhyanty anucitā nāryo videhāni śirāṃsi ca
english: "And seeing the headless trunks and the heads severed from their bodies—a sight that gladdens only the dreadful—the women, unused to such things, swoon away."

sanskrit: śiraḥ kāyena saṃdhāya prekṣamāṇā vicetasaḥ apaśyantyo paraṃ tatra nedam asyeti duḥkhitāḥ
english: "Some, out of their senses, fitting a head to a trunk and gazing upon it, and seeing no more there, sorrow, saying, 'This is not his.'"

sanskrit: bāhūrucaraṇān anyān viśikhonmathitān pṛthak saṃdadhatyo 'sukhāviṣṭā mūrchanty etāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "And others, overcome with anguish, joining together the arms, thighs, and feet that arrows had hewn apart, swoon again and again."

sanskrit: utkṛttaśirasaś cānyān vijagdhān mṛgapakṣibhiḥ dṛṣṭvā kāś cin na jānanti bhartṝn bharatayoṣitaḥ
english: "And seeing others with their heads cut off, devoured by beasts and birds, some women of the Bharatas cannot recognize their own husbands."

sanskrit: pāṇibhiś cāparā ghnanti śirāṃsi madhusūdana prekṣya bhrātṝn pitṝn putrān patīṃś ca nihatān paraiḥ
english: "And others beat their heads with their hands, O slayer of Madhu, beholding their brothers, fathers, sons, and husbands slain by the foe."

sanskrit: bāhubhiś ca sakhaḍgaiś ca śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ agamyakalpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: "With arms still grasping swords, with heads still bearing their earrings, the earth has become well-nigh impassable, a mire of flesh and blood."

sanskrit: na duḥkheṣūcitāḥ pūrvaṃ duḥkhaṃ gāhanty aninditāḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ putrair upakīrṇāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: "These blameless women, never before acquainted with sorrow, now plunge into grief, treading the earth that is strewn with their brothers, their fathers, and their sons."
